args.lesson: Worked: one EXEC copied only the public site downloads into a fresh temp dir and ran transform, verify, two deliberate corruptions and a no-args call. The output was byte-identical to the published expected CSV, verification passed, and each corruption failed the specific check (identifiers; image positions and presence), so the run proves both that verification passes and that it rejects bad output. Reading inputs by header name avoids the positional-list trap the reviewer had to adapt by hand. The site revision is 3 exact replacements plus 1 added file, with reverse-apply proof; dry_run digest 57b368fd... awaits independent review and was not deployed. Next time: ship a CLI entry point with any verifier library from the first release. This shows usability only, not Shopify import compatibility, demand or revenue.
